newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban plan delegation to West.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban plan delegation to West.

text.p: Afghanistan's new Taleban rulers said on Wednesday they planned to send a delegation to the country's neighbours and western nations to ease what they called misunderstandings over their Islamic policies.

Acting deputy foreign minister Sher Mohammad Stanakzai told a news conference that the Islamic purist movement, which took Kabul in late September wanted good relations with all such countries, including the United States and Europe.
"We want also good relations with them. We will try to further increase our relations with them.

"Soon a high-ranking delegation will be nominated on behalf of the Islamic government of Afghanistan; they will travel to the neighbouring countries and maybe they go to Europe and the United States to remove those misunderstandings and establish good relations with them," he said.

Officials denied that Stanakzai had been removed from his position, saying that as acting minister his position had yet to be officially confirmed and was subject to change by the ruling shura, or council.
Taleban sources in Pakistan had said on Tuesday that Stanakzai had been moved to the Ministry of Rehabilitation and Reconstruction as acting deputy minister.

The Taleban's directives placing severe limitations on the role of women, have alarmed western human rights groups and prompted the United States and United Nations to express concern in separate statements on Monday.

Stanakzai and other Taleban officials have said the west's concern is the result of misunderstanding of Taleban policies, although some have defended the directives and said they are not open to the compromise demanded by aid groups.
"I think they have misunderstood our position. We have already declared we are not against the women's rights. In fact it is Islam who has given for the first time rights to the women," he said.
The Taleban would not compromise on its laws concerning women, Stanakzai said, although he added that final directives concerning the role and education of women had yet to be made.

"It's up to the world what the United Nations and other countries want out of us and what they are saying through their mass media. Whatever rules and regulations are in Islam in our society we will go strictly according to that," he said.
